The Police Inspector of R. T. Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4
for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 504, 506 read with sec.34 of Indian Penal Code
an
d Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Prosecution Case:

The marriage of CW1 Smt. Prutvi Jadav and accused No.1 was solemnized on 28-04-2019, at that time the accused No.1 to 4 demanded and received Rs.1 lakh, 60.590 grams of gold ornaments, 909.670 grams of silver articles, household items as dowry and she was residing with accused at No.72, 1st Cross, 2nd Main, Matadahalli within the limits of R.T.Nagara PS.

Thereafter, the accused No.1 to 4 with common intention started ill- treating CW1 and abused her by suspecting her character, not giving her food and thrown her out of the house for want of additional dowry thereby subjected her to mental and physical cruelty.

On 05- 03-2021 when the family of CW1 brought CW1 to her matrimonial house however the accused persons KABC030767912021 CC No.28729/2021 threatened her by stating that if she not fetched the dowry as demanded, she cannot live in the marital house.

After registration of case, CW7 Sri Subaschandra Pattana, PSI of R.T.Nagara Police Station drawn spot mahazar on 18-0-2021 and handed over the case papers to CW8 Sri Ashwath Gowda.G., PI of R.T. 5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offence alleged against the accused No.1 to 4.

The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 8 witnesses and examined 2 witnesses and exhibited 7 documents.

The learned Sr.APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that the PW2 did not supported the case and hence the prosecution side was taken as closed on 05-11-2024 on account of settlement of matrimonial differences amongst PW2 and the accused persons.

sentences.text:
Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 28-04-2019 accused married CW1 Pritvi Jadav, at that time the accused No.1 to 4 demanded and received Rs.1 lakh,
60.590 grams of gold ornaments, 909.670 grams of silver articles, household items from parents of CW1 as dowry thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable under Sec.3 of D.P. Act?

KABC030767912021 CC No.28729/2021 2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage they were residing wherein the accused persons were residing at No.72, 1st Cross, 2nd Main, Matadahalli within the limits of R.T.Nagara PS., at that time the accused No.1 to 4 with common intention picked up quarrel with CW1 and subjected her to both physically and mentally cruelty thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable under Sec.498(A) R/W sec.34 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt at above said house the accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention abused CW1 in filthiest language knowingly such abusive words will provoke breach of peace thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec. 504 R/w Sec.34 of IPC?

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 28-05-2022 above said place, in furtherance of common intention the accused No.1 to 4 threatened CW1 with dire consequences thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC?
5. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said duration accused persons harassed CW1 to fetch additional dowry from her parents thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.4 of D.P.Act?
6. What order?
13. The findings on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1-5 : In the Negative  Point No.6 : As per final order  KABC030767912021 CC No.28729/2021  REASONS Pruthvi Jadav N.R vs Mithilesh E on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171576855/

sentences.text: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined two witnesses, which is as follows:
i.

CW6 Sri Shashiprasad, the then PSI of R.T.Nagara PS examined as PW1 deposed that, on 17-04-2011 he received the written complaint from CW1 as per Ex.P1,
registered the case, prepared FIR as per Ex.P2 and send to the court and handed over the case papers to CW7.

He identified his signatures as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a).
ii. CW1 by name Smt. Prutvi Jadav being Informant examined as PW2 identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (complaint), Ex.P3 seizure mahazar and Ex.P4 Rough Sketch as Ex.P1(b), 3(a) and 4(a).

She further stated that when she went to police station for settlement of minor differences of opinion amongst her and accused No.1, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and 3.

In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined this KABC030767912021 CC No.28729/2021 witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.
She has identified mediation agreements and decree of divorce as per Ex.P5 to 7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, PW1 is police official who has deposed about the registration of FIR only, which is formal in nature, hence his evidence is not useful to case of prosecution.
PW2 is the informant cum victim did not support the prosecution case.
Though the prosecution has cross examined her by treating as hostile witness, no favorable answers has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.
However it appears from the cross examination of PW2 that the disputes between the accused No. 1 and her in M.C.No. 2820/2021 have been settled.

. The learned APP argued that the Section 498A of Indian Penal code is not compoundable offence as per section 320 of CRPC and hence the examination of witnesses is necessary however this court dispensed the same on account of amicable settlement arrived between the rival parties to the case and PW2 did not support the prosecution case.
Yes this court agrees with the view of the Learned Sr.APP that the section 498A of IPC cannot be compounded as per Section 320 of CRPC.

This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR IN THE MATTER OF AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. This court further places reliance upon the decision in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the KABC030767912021 CC No.28729/2021 matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
18.
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW2 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498A of I.P.C. is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW2 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

KABC030767912021 CC No.28729/2021 Pruthvi Jadav N.R vs Mithilesh E on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171576855/
6 19.

entities.text: Pruthvi Jadav N.R vs Mithilesh E
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".
20.

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
In this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the offence under section 498A of IPC with other offences under section 504, 506 of IPC cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 5 in the Negative.

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 5, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 to 4 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A), 504, 506 read with Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
